New York rapper Cardi B has released a new single titled "Ah Ha," her first solo music since the release of her 2025 album, Am I the Drama?. The track was produced by DJ SwanQo and features Cardi's signature humor and sass. Notably, she includes the line "na na na boo boo" in the lyrics.

This single marks a return to form for Cardi B after embarking on an arena tour in support of her second album last year. She also performed two songs from the record, including “Bodega Baddie” and “ErrTime,” on Saturday Night Live earlier this year.

The release comes as part of Cardi's ongoing musical career, which has seen her perform alongside other notable artists such as Billie Eilish at Coachella 2021. With "Ah Ha," Cardi appears to be continuing the momentum from her recent success and is likely aiming to solidify her position in the music industry once again.

Kanye West faced accusations of using AI in Vultures 2 Mark Hale https://indiefferential.com/kanye-west-vultures-2/ 2026-08-16T23:58:20+03:00 The producer, whose suit was filed anonymously in Los Angeles’ Superior Court, alleges that he was brought in “on an emergency basis” just two days before Vultures 2’s release. He contends that his work included creating at least 13 custom AI voice models and more…

The producer, whose suit was filed anonymously in Los Angeles’ Superior Court, alleges that he was brought in “on an emergency basis” just two days before Vultures 2’s release. He contends that his work included creating at least 13 custom AI voice models and more than 400 individual vocal generations, based on his own voice. The producer claims to have contributed further AI vocal programming to West's most recent solo album, Bully, starting in October 2024.

His suit alleges he has not yet been paid for his work on both Bully and Vultures 2, nor have he and his label, YZY, included him in the production credits on streaming platforms. He seeks at least $110,000 in breach of contract, unjust enrichment, and violations of California’s Unfair Competition Law and the Los Angeles Freelance Worker Protections Ordinance.

West had previously stated that Bully used no AI technology, despite his acknowledgment of using it in songwriting and recording. Last week, West settled a 2024 lawsuit brought against him by Lauren Pisciotta, who accused him of sexual assault and harassment. Another recent court case involving an uncleared sample on the Donda track "Hurricane" ended in favor of the plaintiff, with West ordered to pay just under $200,000.

Vultures 2 was released in 2024, following allegations of AI manipulation. The producer’s lawsuit brings renewed scrutiny to Kanye West's use of technology in his music production.

Karol G Surprises Fans with Bruno Mars Collaboration During Los Angeles Show Mark Hale https://indiefferential.com/karol-g-surprises-fans-with-bruno-mars-collaboration-during-los-angeles-show/ 2026-08-16T23:11:20+03:00 During Karol G’s second sold-out show at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium, the Colombian superstar brought out her collaborator Bruno Mars for a live performance of their new collaboration, “Still,” from Karol G’s latest studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. During Karol G’s second sold-out show at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium, the Colombian superstar brought out her collaborator Bruno Mars for a live performance of their new collaboration, “Still,” from Karol G’s latest studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. The track debuted on Billboard’s Hot 100 in March and features the pair harmonizing about unconditional love despite no longer being together.

The event was notable not only for the performance but also as it marked the filming of “Still”’s music video. Fans were informed through a large video screen that they would be witnessing the song’s official recording right then and there with Karol G and Bruno Mars, who wore matching outfits for added impact.

Karol G opened the power ballad in a sparkling white dress before being joined by Bruno Mars, who sported a flower-embroidered white suit adorned with a cowboy hat. The pair then performed “Still,” the opening track from Bruno Mars’ upcoming album, The Romantic.

The new single has received positive reception, as Karol G revealed she posted a TikTok video discussing it and how it expressed her current emotions naturally without feeling pressured to use another language. "There’s a song on the album that’s entirely in English," she said, emphasizing the importance of organic expression in music creation.

Twenty One Pilots Set to Debut UK Concert at Victoria Park George S. https://indiefferential.com/twenty-one-pilots-set-to-debut-uk-concert-at-victoria-park/ 2026-08-16T23:10:20+03:00 The Grammy Award-winning duo Twenty One Pilots are set to make their debut performance in the United Kingdom at London's Victoria Park on Sunday, August 30. This will be the only UK concert of the year for the band, and they have lined up a…

The Grammy Award-winning duo Twenty One Pilots are set to make their debut performance in the United Kingdom at London's Victoria Park on Sunday, August 30. This will be the only UK concert of the year for the band, and they have lined up a stellar supporting act including Wunderhorse, Nova Twins, and more. 

To add an extra layer of engagement with their fans, the band's creative and content director, Mark C. Eshleman, is inviting about 10 lucky attendees to capture footage from the concert using both Hi-8 and miniDV cameras. These fans will document not only their fan life but also their journey to the show, which will be woven into a feature film that will be released later.

In anticipation of this event, Twenty One Pilots recently released "More Than We Ever Imagined," a concert film capturing their performance at the Mexico City venue during their 'The Clancy World Tour.' The band provided commentary throughout the video to reflect on their journey from early shows to becoming career milestones.

Earlier in the year, they performed a headline set at Mad Cool Festival in Madrid and were described by NME as "the latest in a long line of theatrical performances" with fireworks and pyrotechnics illuminating the stage. Recently, the band has been hitting European festival stages, including stops in Budapest.

The concert also featured a surprise performance from Jack White, who gave permission for Tyler Joseph and Josh Dun to include a sing-along of "Seven Nation Army," which added an extra touch of magic to their show.

In a Los Angeles courtroom Friday, lawyers for reggaeton superstar Bad Bunny and other major artists in the genre faced off with those representing Steely & Clevie, the duo behind the 1989 song "Fish Market," in a high-stakes copyright dispute. The case hinges on whether a combination of musical elements from multiple songs infringe upon the composition copyright for "Fish Market."

In July, U.S. District Judge André Birotte Jr. found that more than 1,800 reggaeton songs by nearly 100 artists potentially infringed on the original dembow rhythm pattern in "Fish Market." The plaintiffs claim this rhythm is integral to defining the genre.

Bad Bunny’s lead lawyer, Kenneth Freundlich, argued at Friday's hearing that Steely & Clevie did not own the composition copyright for "Pounder (Dub Mix II)," which includes a two-bar timbale loop. Freundlich pointed out that while Browne testified in court, he claimed the pattern came from two separate portions of "Fish Market," rather than being a single, continuous two-measure figure as alleged by plaintiffs.

Freundlich also noted that Steely & Clevie do not hold the composition copyright for "Pounder," only its sound recording. He accused the plaintiffs of claiming exclusive rights to a "complete blur" of elements taken from different songs, likening it to taking a slice from one painting and repeating it in another.

In response, plaintiffs’ lawyer Benjamin Tookey countered that Steely & Clevie did indeed own composition copyright for "Fish Market," and their defense was based on the presence of the two-bar timbale pattern within the song. He claimed this dispute is akin to someone claiming a piece from one painting as part of another, which is not accurate.

U.S. District Judge André Birotte Jr., who issued the July ruling, expressed his intention to review the matter further, citing that he needed "to mull this nightmare over some more." The judge took the case under submission and said it would likely take several weeks before issuing a decision.

Bad Bunny’s lawyers filed for reconsideration of the July ruling or an immediate appeal. Freundlich argued that taking the dispute to trial would be impractical, given the extensive discovery process required to examine 1,800 songs by scores of famous artists including Karol G and Daddy

Coles https://indiefferential.com/californias-bid-to-curb-live-event-ticket-resale-prices-dies-in-session/ 2026-08-16T12:59:26+03:00 California’s attempt to cap live event ticket resale prices at 10% above face value was put on hold for the current legislative session. The California Senate Appropriations Committee held AB 1720, known as the California Fans First Act, on its suspense file on August 13,…

California’s attempt to cap live event ticket resale prices at 10% above face value was put on hold for the current legislative session. The California Senate Appropriations Committee held AB 1720, known as the California Fans First Act, on its suspense file on August 13, one day before the deadline for state fiscal committees to report bills to the floor.

The bill, introduced in February by San Francisco Assemblymember Matt Haney, aimed to limit resale prices of concert and live event tickets to 10% above face value, including fees. It would have also capped fees charged by resale marketplaces. The measure was amended in May to cover only independent venues with capacities under 3,000, plus certain nonprofit venues.

The bill defined an independent venue as one that derives a majority of its revenue from ticket events and is not majority-owned by a publicly traded company or operates more than 10 states. Professional sports and athletic events were exempted from the measure.

California’s Department of Justice estimated the cost of enforcing AB 1720 at around $1.6 million in fiscal year 2026–27, decreasing to about $582,000 annually thereafter. The state's Department of Finance opposed the bill at an Appropriations hearing on August 3, citing enforcement costs and the potential burden on California courts.

Asm. Matt Haney, who championed the bill, stated in a statement that he would continue pushing for solutions to address ticket resale practices. He emphasized that artists across genres have called for such measures and cited examples of other states and countries already adopting similar caps to curb predatory resale practices while allowing resales when necessary.

Despite not being able to carry over into the next session, Haney indicated his intention to reintroduce a new bill once the Legislature reconvenes in December. Ron Gubitz, Executive Director of the Music Artists Coalition, expressed gratitude for Asm. Haney's advocacy but noted that protecting fans at every show remains essential.

Suno Studio Launches 2.0 With Enhanced Features Mark Hale https://indiefferential.com/suno-studio-launches-20-with-enhanced-features/ 2026-08-16T12:58:26+03:00 AI music company Suno announced the launch of Studio 2.0, a significant update to its browser-based digital audio workstation (DAW). AI music company Suno announced the launch of Studio 2.0, a significant update to its browser-based digital audio workstation (DAW). The new version includes features such as MIDI support, a beta AI chat bar, and advanced stem separation, along with new audio effects and automations.

Suno emphasizes that “Grammy-winning artists” have used Suno Studio in the past to create chart-topping hits. However, the company has also implemented stricter download limits for its free users. Free users will be limited to seven downloads per lifetime account, while Pro subscribers (at $8–$10 a month) and Premier subscribers (at $24–$30 a month) are restricted to 20 and 60 monthly downloads, respectively.

Despite these changes, Suno Studio, available only to its Premier subscribers, will have no download limits. This move reflects Suno’s commitment to supporting musicians who use the platform for professional purposes.

Henry Phipps, Suno’s Studio Product Manager, highlighted in a blog post that “perhaps our biggest takeaway from spending time with artists is their deep appreciation for the instruments and tools that have earned a place in their studios.” He emphasized the importance of maintaining access to traditional music foundations like guitars, drum machines, synths, effects, and step sequencers within the next generation of music software.

Suno Studio 2.0’s most requested addition, MIDI support, allows users to import, record, and edit MIDI on the timeline. In a unique feature, MIDI clips can also be used as prompts for new audio generations generated by Studio. The chat bar, launching in beta, lets users interact with Suno “like you would any other collaborator,” suggesting it can create instruments and vocals, build custom plugins, or even tidy up sessions.

Phipps noted that text prompts are useful for finding inspiration but emphasized that they are no substitute for playing a part on a MIDI keyboard or recording with a microphone. The chat feature is described as a tool to help musicians collaborate more effectively within the platform.

Courtney Love has provided an update on her upcoming album, revealing that it is complete and a "really good record." The musician also addressed the health scare she experienced in 2019. In a video posted to Instagram, Love mentioned moving from Los Angeles to London, which prompted her to shift away from social media for a few weeks.

She detailed how her body "exploded" during her illness and that she was frequently hospitalized. Describing herself as about 100 pounds lighter and losing all her hair, Love said doctors told her she might die. Despite the severity of her condition, she stated that she never believed them and managed to recover.

Love then spoke about how these experiences influenced her new album, mentioning instances where adults would confuse colors with her. She explained her struggle to cope with such contradictions in perception, which she believes relates to many fans' collective understanding. "I never really lost my ability to see red as red," she said, acknowledging the mental health struggles and coping mechanisms that played a role in her artistic output.

In closing, Love referenced Hole's 2010 album, Nobody’s Daughter, noting how it received significant criticism upon its release. She described an instance where they performed at Pizza Hut Park at 11 AM while Limp Bizkit was headlining with 30 Seconds to Mars, describing the experience as "spectacularly humbling."

Effective immediately, Slipknot has severed ties with turntablist Sid Wilson, according to a social media post by the band, which was shared by Stereogum on August 14. The post read: “We wish him the best in his future endeavors.” No official comments were provided by the band regarding this decision.

Wilson joined Slipknot in 1998 and served as both keyboardist and turntablist. His departure follows a series of recent changes within the group, including Chris Fehn’s parting ways with Slipknot in 2019 due to unpaid claims he made, Craig Jones’ exit from the band in 2023 after serving for nearly two decades as a keyboardist and sampler, and Jay Weinberg leaving the band that year following creative differences.

The departure of these key members underscores ongoing personnel changes within Slipknot. In April, drummer Jay Weinberg spoke with Rolling Stone about his experience parting ways from the band, noting he sought to learn from this experience in future creative endeavors where he hoped to find greater camaraderie and respect among colleagues.
